# Importance Sampling (IMP)

> **Maturity: beta** — see [Feature Maturity](../maturity.qmd) for what this means.

`imp` is, **by default, a Monte-Carlo EM estimator** — the equivalent of
NONMEM `$EST METHOD=IMP`. It maximises the importance-sampled marginal
likelihood, updating θ/Ω/σ each iteration. Set `imp_eval_only = true`
(NONMEM `EONLY=1`) to instead *evaluate* the marginal log-likelihood

$$
-2 \log L(\theta) \;=\; -2 \sum_i \log p(y_i \mid \theta)
\;=\; -2 \sum_i \log \int p(y_i \mid \eta, \theta)\, p(\eta \mid \theta)\, d\eta
$$

at the **fixed** input parameters without estimating them.

> **⚠️ Behaviour change.** Before this release `imp` only *evaluated*
> `−2 log L` at fixed parameters (the `imp_eval_only` behaviour). It is now an
> estimator by default. If you used `method = imp` (or `[focei, imp]`) purely to
> *score* a fit, add `imp_eval_only = true` to keep the old behaviour.

## Mapping to NONMEM

| ferx | NONMEM |
|------|--------|
| `method = imp` (default) | `$EST METHOD=IMP` (estimator) |
| `method = imp` + `imp_eval_only = true` | `$EST METHOD=IMP EONLY=1` (evaluate) |
| `method = impmap` | `$EST METHOD=IMPMAP` (estimator) |

The IS Monte-Carlo estimator of `p(yᵢ|θ)` is unbiased; the reported `−2 log L`
carries a Jensen bias from the `log(·)` transform that vanishes as `K → ∞`. That
bias is small only while the proposal covers the posterior, which is why ferx
[adapts the proposal](#adaptive-evaluation) before it reports a marginal.

## How the estimator works

IMP is a Monte-Carlo EM (MCEM) loop sharing all of its machinery with
[IMPMAP](impmap.qmd) except the **proposal re-centering strategy**:

- On the **first** iteration it finds each subject's conditional mode and
  first-order variance via a FOCE inner loop, and centres the
  importance-sampling proposal there.
- On **every subsequent** iteration it re-centres the proposal from the
  *previous* iteration's importance-sample mean and covariance — it does **not**
  re-run the inner loop. This is the one-line difference from IMPMAP (which
  re-derives the mode/variance every iteration) and the source of IMP's
  lower per-iteration cost.

Each iteration's M-step updates θ/Ω/σ from the importance-weighted posterior
moments (closed-form Ω and log-mu-referenced θ; a small BOBYQA step for σ and
non-mu-ref θ), exactly as in IMPMAP. The reported estimate is the running mean
of the parameter vector over the final `imp_averaging` iterations, and `ofv` is
a final FOCE Laplace pass for AIC/BIC comparability.

> **Which number matches NONMEM's reported OFV?** NONMEM `METHOD=IMP` reports the
> importance-sampling Monte-Carlo **marginal** `−2 log L` (the `.ext`/`.lst`
> `#OBJV`), *not* a Laplace value. ferx's `ofv` is a Laplace pass, so it will
> **not** equal NONMEM's IMP `#OBJV` on data where the Laplace approximation and
> the true marginal diverge (sparse / strongly nonlinear). The NONMEM-comparable
> number is the marginal, evaluated at the final estimates and surfaced on
> `FitResult.importance_sampling.minus2_log_likelihood` (with its Monte-Carlo SE
> on `.mc_standard_error`) for **estimating** `imp`/`impmap` runs too — not only
> the evaluation-only path. If IMPMAP is configured with a Gaussian proposal
> (`impmap_proposal_df = normal`), it is replaced by a finite-`t` proposal for
> this final marginal eval, so the heavier tails keep the importance weights bounded.
> `imp` makes no such substitution: `imp_proposal_df = normal` is used as given.

The console report and the fit YAML label both numbers. In R, the marginal is
`fit$importance_sampling$minus2_log_likelihood`. AIC and BIC come from `ofv`, so
they differ from NONMEM's IMP objective in the same way. The console report prints:

```
OFV (Laplace):  4326.6000
IS marginal -2LL:  4299.6000  (MC SE = 0.7500, K = 1000)
AIC:  4340.6000
BIC:  4371.2000
OFV, AIC and BIC come from a final Laplace pass, not the IS marginal.
Compare NONMEM METHOD=IMP objectives with the IS marginal, not OFV.
```

and the YAML `objective_function` block adds `ofv_type: laplace`,
`marginal_minus2_log_likelihood` and `marginal_mc_standard_error`. `ofv` itself
keeps its value and key. If the marginal evaluation was skipped, a warning gives
the reason and the marginal rows are absent. `ferx summary` labels `ofv` the same
way but shows no marginal, because a `.fitrx` file does not store it.

An `imp_eval_only` stage after an estimator leaves that estimator's objective in
`ofv`, so `ofv` gets no Laplace label there, and the marginal is printed beside it
all the same. A trailing `agq_eval_only` stage replaces `ofv` with its quadrature
marginal, and the label is dropped for the same reason.

### Adaptive sample count

`imp_auto` and `impmap_auto` are on by default, so `imp_samples` and
`impmap_samples` are starting counts, and K never goes below them. After each
iteration K may rise, up to 10000, while the **per-subject** objective Monte-Carlo
SE exceeds 0.05. The SE used is the median of the last five iterations, rescaled to
the current K, because a single iteration's SE follows the few worst-sampled subjects:

$$
\frac{\operatorname{SE}(-2 \log L_{IS})}{\sqrt{N}} \;>\; 0.05
$$

A rise waits until one of two things is true:

- **The objective has settled.** The means of the last two 5-iteration windows differ
  by no more than two standard errors of that difference, taken from the total
  MC SE. Early in a run the proposal lags the parameters, so the SE reflects that lag
  and says little about what the converged fit needs.
- **The averaging window is about to start**, so the iterations behind the reported
  estimate are sampled to the target even on a fit that never settles. The hold
  covers at least the first half of the run and at most the first three quarters.

Each rise aims for the K the SE asks for, since SE² scales as 1/K, plus 10% headroom,
and at most doubles K. When the SE falls below 0.025, K halves.

K also stops rising when samples stop paying for themselves. If SE² scales as 1/K,
then SE²·K stays constant, so once it has doubled since the first rise that
assumption has failed and following the SE would only walk K to the cap. On
`cefepime_jordan` the SE was 0.071 at K = 1000 and 0.083 at K = 6912. If the
product falls back, rises resume. A fit that ends noisy after this stop says so in
its warnings, and a larger `imp_samples` is unlikely to help it.

A subject whose importance weights are degenerate, with ESS below 2 because one draw
carries all the weight or because its sampler failed, adds about 1 to the variance
sum whatever K is. One such subject keeps the per-subject SE above 0.05 for any N
below 1600, so it could ramp every subject to the cap without improving itself. A
degenerate subject still counts at first, since a proposal that only undersamples
the posterior recovers as K grows. It is left out of the decision once, over consecutive
degenerate iterations, K has risen above the lowest K of that run and the subject is
still degenerate; a lowering of K does not count. A failed subject is left out at
once. When the set left out changes, the five-iteration SE window is recomputed
without them, so they stop driving rises straight away. The fit's warning names the subjects left out at the
final iteration: they need a better proposal (check their EBE and Hessian), not more
samples. The reported MC SE still includes them.

The per-subject form keeps the rule from ramping a large
dataset purely because it has more subjects, since the total SE grows as √N. NONMEM's
`AUTO` targets the total: `STDOBJ = 1.0` corresponds to 0.05 only near N = 400. With
100 subjects the ferx rule asks for a total SE of 0.5, half of NONMEM's target, so
it can sample far more than NONMEM would on the same model.

A model that stays above the target ramps to the cap and runs there, at about ten
times the per-iteration cost of K = 1000. If a run is too slow, set
`imp_auto = false` to pin `imp_samples`. The fit then warns if the final per-subject
MC SE is above 0.1. The cap and target are fixed.

The final marginal uses the configured `imp_samples` / `impmap_samples`, not the
ramped K, so its `K` and MC SE describe that one evaluation. To tighten the MC SE
of the reported marginal, raise the starting count.

### Wall-clock limit

`imp_max_time` and `impmap_max_time` cap the MCEM iterations, in seconds. The limit is
checked after each iteration, so the iteration in progress finishes. A fit that reaches
the limit stops there and keeps its result:

- The estimate is the mean of the averaging iterations reached, or the last iteration's
  parameters if the averaging window had not started.
- `converged` is `false`, and a warning gives the iteration reached.
- The post-fit work still runs: final EBEs, the covariance step if enabled, and the
  marginal evaluation. It is not counted against the limit, so set `covariance = false`
  if the budget is tight.

The limit covers the IMP or IMPMAP stage alone, not earlier stages of a chain such as
`[focei, imp]`. Where a fit stops depends on the machine, so a run that reaches the
limit is not reproducible from its seed.

### Rich data and cold starts

IMP's proposal lags one iteration behind the parameters, so the bookkeeping
between iterations matters. The closed-form mu-ref step moves each packed θ by
the population mean of η, and the posterior of η moves the other way by the same
amount. ferx translates each subject's stored importance draws with it — the
samples and their weighted mean, per class under a mixture — so the proposal stays on the
posterior while the individual parameters do not change. Each #619 group step
does the same with its own shift. The samples move as well as the moments
because a later group step in the same iteration, under `impmap` too, scores
them at the already-shifted θ.

Until #1365 those stored means were left where they were. From a cold start the
first step is several posterior SDs, so on iteration 2 every subject went
low-ESS and the fit diverged. That collapse was read as IMP's inherent rich-data
weakness, but it was this bookkeeping gap. Measured cold-start runs, as the
importance-sampling −2 log L at the last iteration (macOS arm64):

| Model, iterations | before | after | reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `examples/warfarin.ferx`, 50 | 1.4e15, every subject low-ESS | −286.0 | NONMEM `METHOD=IMP` −285.69 |
| `examples/two_cpt_oral_cov.ferx`, 30 | 4.8e14, every subject low-ESS | −1199.6 | `[focei, imp]` −1199.4 |
| FREM warfarin fixture (`tests/frem_warfarin.rs`), 3 | +328.8 | −151.6 | 60 iterations reach −220.9; SAEM / IMPMAP −220.7 |

A warm start (`method = [focei, imp]`) still saves iterations. A subject whose
posterior is very sharp can still lose overlap after a large step in a parameter
the shift does not own (a non-mu-referenced θ, σ, or Ω), and
[`impmap`](impmap.qmd), which re-centres on the mode every iteration, is the
robust choice when the low-ESS count stays high.

```
[fit_options]
  method        = imp            # estimate by importance-sampling MCEM
  imp_iterations = 200            # MCEM iterations
  imp_samples    = 1000           # K, samples per subject per iteration
  imp_averaging  = 50             # terminal iterations to average
  imp_proposal_df = 5             # ν, Student-t tail weight (or `normal` → MVN)
  imp_seed       = 12345
```

```
[fit_options]
  method = [focei, imp]          # robust on rich data: warm-start IMP from FOCEI
```

## Evaluation-only mode (`imp_eval_only = true`)

With `imp_eval_only = true`, `imp` does **not** estimate: it evaluates the IS
`−2 log L` at the fixed input parameters and reports it on
`FitResult.importance_sampling` (handy for scoring imported / fixed parameter
sets, or comparing models on a lower-bias likelihood than the Laplace OFV).

### When evaluation-only is useful

The Laplace approximation behind the FOCE/FOCEI OFV assumes each subject's
posterior of η is Gaussian-shaped — fine for **well-sampled** PK (≥ 5–6 obs
per subject) but biased for **sparse data**, **strong nonlinearity**
(Michaelis–Menten, TMDD, transit absorption), or **categorical/binary PD**.
There the FOCE OFV is typically *under*-stated, so naïve AIC/BIC favours
over-parameterised models; the IS `−2 log L` is much lower-bias.

```
[fit_options]
  method        = [focei, imp]   # estimate with FOCEI, then score the IS-LL
  imp_eval_only  = true
  imp_samples    = 2000
  imp_proposal_df = 5
```

```
[fit_options]
  method       = imp             # standalone: IS-LL at the initial parameters
  imp_eval_only = true
```

Rules for the **evaluation-only** mode:

- **Standalone is allowed.** `method = imp` + `imp_eval_only` evaluates the IS-LL
  at the **initial parameters** — deriving the EBEs/Jacobian (the proposal
  centre/scale) there via a FOCE inner loop. When chained after an estimator
  (`[focei, imp]`), it uses that stage's EBEs/Jacobian instead.
- **Must appear at most once** (true for both modes).
- **Must be terminal.** `method = [imp, focei]` with `imp_eval_only` is rejected
  — a following stage would overwrite the parameters and make the IS result
  meaningless. (The *estimating* `imp` has no such restriction; it may lead or
  sit mid-chain like any estimator.)

For the estimating `imp`, `FitResult.method` reports `IMP`. For an
evaluation-only `imp` after an estimator it reports that estimating stage (e.g.
`FOCEI`); standalone evaluation-only reports `IMP`. Either way
`FitResult.method_chain` preserves the full chain, and the IS-LL lands on
`FitResult.importance_sampling`.

## Adaptive evaluation {#adaptive-evaluation}

Every reported marginal, whether from `imp_eval_only` or at the end of an
estimating `imp` or `impmap` stage, first adapts each subject's proposal. The
MCEM iterations themselves are not affected.

- **Pilot passes.** `imp_adapt_passes` (default 5) passes each draw K samples
  from the current proposal and re-centre it on their weighted mean and
  covariance, as NONMEM does across `NITER` under `EONLY=1`. A pass with too few
  effective draws to estimate a covariance (fewer than 2(d + 1) for d sampled
  random effects) stops there and keeps the last good proposal.
- **Fresh final draws.** The pilots only choose the proposal, and the reported
  marginal comes from K new draws, so it stays unbiased.
- **A prior component.** The final proposal and the pilots keep at least 10% of
  the prior `N(0, Ω)`, as in the [defensive mixture](#defensive-mixture); a larger
  `imp_defensive_alpha` is kept. Re-centring cannot reach a second mode, and
  the prior's bounded weights can.

Each pass costs one more K draws per subject, so the default evaluation costs 6×
the single-proposal one (pembrolizumab, K = 3000: 1.9 s to 12.7 s per evaluation
on 6 threads). `imp_adapt_passes = 0` restores the single Laplace proposal with
`imp_defensive_alpha` as set. On a FREM Rao-Blackwellised subject the prior
component applies but the pilots do not run; its low-dimensional conditional
proposal is already well matched.

### Why a proposal built at the mode reads high

On a very sparse subject the posterior of a poorly informed η can run along a
long ridge or hold a second mode, and a proposal built from the mode and its
curvature never reaches that mass. The missing mass lowers `log p̂`, so the
marginal reads **high**. The MC SE comes from the same draws, so it does not show
the gap, and it shrinks as slowly as the bias does: on cefepime the ESS of the
worst subjects *falls* as K grows, because rare tail draws start to appear.

Measured on cefepime (458 subjects, 702 observations, 3 ETAs, macOS arm64) at
NONMEM's FOCEI estimates. The reference is an independent estimate, drawn from a
proposal at the prior scale so that the weights are bounded.

| Evaluator | K | −2 log L |
|---|---:|---:|
| Reference (prior-scale proposal) | 10⁶ | 4297.24 ± 0.11 |
| ferx, adaptive (default) | 1000 | 4297.07 ± 1.34 |
| ferx, adaptive (default) | 3000 | 4297.06 ± 0.50 |
| ferx, `imp_adapt_passes = 0` | 3000 | 4306.54 ± 2.47 |
| ferx, `imp_adapt_passes = 0` | 30000 | 4299.83 ± 3.74 |
| NONMEM 7.5.1 `EONLY=1 NITER=5`, normal proposal | 3000 | 4301.84 ± 0.94 |
| NONMEM, same, last pass of one run | 30000 | 4299.2 |
| NONMEM, same with `DF=4`, last pass of one run | 3000 | 4297.2 |
| NONMEM, same with `DF=4`, last pass of one run | 30000 | 4297.5 |

The ferx rows are the mean ± SD over six seeds, and the reference and the
3000-sample NONMEM row over three. So on data this sparse ferx reads **below** NONMEM's default `EONLY=1`
run, and NONMEM's default is the one that is high: give NONMEM a heavy-tailed
proposal (`DF=4`) and the two agree. Compare against that, not against the
default normal proposal. At a second parameter point on the same model the
reference is 4275.0, ferx reads 4275.3 ± 1.6 at K = 1000, and NONMEM's default
reads 4282.7.

On the six other models tested the default stays within 0.4 of NONMEM's
`EONLY=1` at K = 3000 (warfarin, thioguanine, infliximab, vancomycin, propofol,
pembrolizumab), and the worst-subject ESS / K rises on all but warfarin
(propofol: 0.011 to 0.59).

### When the marginal is still unreliable

If the worst subject ends with fewer than 10 effective draws, the fit adds a
warning to `FitResult.warnings`: the marginal tends to read high and the MC SE
understates the error. Raise `imp_samples`, and turn adaptation back on if it was
off.

## Algorithm

This is the per-subject importance-sampling kernel — the E-step of the
estimator and the whole of the evaluation-only mode. The estimating loop simply
re-runs this kernel each iteration (re-centring the proposal from the previous
iteration's sample moments) and feeds the weighted moments into the M-step. An
[adaptive evaluation](#adaptive-evaluation) runs it once per pilot pass, then once
more for the reported marginal.

For each subject *i* with proposal centre η̂ᵢ (the EBE on the first
iteration, and at the start of an evaluation) and inner-loop Jacobian
Jᵢ = ∂f/∂η at η̂ᵢ:

1. **Build proposal scale Σᵢ:**
   - Compute Sheiner–Beal posterior Hessian
     $H_i = J_i^\top R_i^{-1} J_i + \Omega^{-1}$ at η̂ᵢ
     ($R_i$ = diagonal residual variance at the EBE).
   - Add a small ridge $\lambda I$ for numerical safety
     (λ = max(10⁻⁶ · trace(H)/d, 10⁻¹⁰)).
   - Cholesky-factor; on failure fall back to Σᵢ = Ω (broad prior-scale
     proposal — gives a valid but noisy LL estimate).

2. **Draw K samples** $\eta_{ik} \sim t_\nu(\hat\eta_i, \Sigma_i)$
   (multivariate Student-t; a multivariate normal with
   `imp_proposal_df = normal`). With `imp_defensive_alpha > 0` a fraction
   of the draws come from the prior (see [Defensive mixture](#defensive-mixture)).
   An IOV subject samples the stacked (η, κ) vector the same way.

3. **Compute log importance weights:**
$$
\log w_{ik} = \log p(y_i \mid \eta_{ik}, \theta)
                + \log p(\eta_{ik} \mid \theta)
                - \log q(\eta_{ik}).
$$

4. **Subject marginal LL** via log-sum-exp:
$$
\log \hat p(y_i \mid \theta)
   \;=\; \operatorname{lse}_k \log w_{ik} - \log K.
$$

5. **Per-subject effective sample size:**
   $\mathrm{ESS}_i = 1 / \sum_k \tilde w_{ik}^2$ (normalised weights).
   The result reports the across-subject min and median of ESS/K, plus
   any subjects below `imp_low_ess_threshold` (default 10%).

6. **Monte-Carlo standard error.** For a self-normalised IS estimator the
   asymptotic per-subject variance (Geweke 1989) is
$$
\operatorname{Var}\bigl(\log \hat p(y_i \mid \theta)\bigr)
   \;\approx\; \frac{1}{K}\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{ESS}_i / K} - 1\right).
$$
   Aggregating across subjects (LL is a sum of independent per-subject
   log-marginals) and converting to the `−2 log L` scale,
$$
\operatorname{SE}(-2 \log L_{IS})
   \;=\; 2 \sqrt{\sum_i \operatorname{Var}\bigl(\log \hat p(y_i \mid \theta)\bigr)}.
$$
   Subjects with degenerate ESS ($\mathrm{ESS}_i / K = 0$ — complete
   proposal collapse) fall back to a per-subject variance of `1.0`, which
   produces a *finite* but inflated SE rather than a NaN. A separate
   warning is emitted on `FitResult.warnings` listing the collapsed
   subjects; the IS-LL itself remains usable as a point estimate.

7. **Population −2 log L** = `−2 · Σᵢ log p̂(yᵢ | θ)`, reported on
   `FitResult.importance_sampling.minus2_log_likelihood` together with
   `mc_standard_error`.

## Tuning

- **`imp_iterations` / `imp_averaging`** (estimator only) set the number of MCEM
  iterations and how many terminal iterations are averaged into the reported
  estimate. Defaults 200 / 50. Under-running shows up as estimates still drifting
  with the MC noise; raise `imp_iterations` if the trace hasn't stabilised.
- **K = `imp_samples`** controls accuracy. The MC SE scales as
  $1/\sqrt{K}$; halve it by quadrupling K.
  Default 1000 is fine for a smoke test; bump to 2000–5000 for any
  reported LL.
- **ν = `imp_proposal_df`** controls the proposal tails. The default of 5
  is robust to mild proposal misspecification (Geweke 1989); raise
  toward 30+ to recover a near-Gaussian proposal when the posterior is
  known to be light-tailed. `normal` (or `mvn`) uses a true
  multivariate-normal proposal, which is the closest match to NONMEM. Its
  light tails make it the less forgiving choice when the posterior is not
  close to Gaussian, so watch ESS and the MC SE.
- **Low-ESS subjects** signal a proposal that doesn't match the posterior
  well, which can mean the EBE didn't converge or the Hessian was near-singular,
  or that the posterior is genuinely not Gaussian. The marginal then tends to read
  [high rather than just noisy](#why-a-proposal-built-at-the-mode-reads-high).
  Investigate by re-running with a tighter `inner_tol` or inspecting the
  `FitResult.subjects[i]` diagnostics.
- **`imp_adapt_passes`** sets how many pilot passes adapt the proposal before a
  marginal is reported. See [Adaptive evaluation](#adaptive-evaluation).
- **Reproducibility.** `imp_seed` defaults to `42` when unset (so two
  fits with the same `imp_samples` and `imp_proposal_df` produce identical
  `−2 log L`). Set it explicitly to vary the RNG stream. The full set of
  `imp_*` defaults is listed in the
  [`[fit_options]` reference](../model-file/fit-options.qmd#importance-sampling-imp).

## When the marginal shows a collapse {#marginal-collapse}

IMP and IMPMAP run a fixed iteration schedule, so `converged` has no stopping
test to report. It rests on the objectives instead. `ofv` is a Laplace pass, which
can look sane on a run that has collapsed, so `fit()` also checks the marginal
in `importance_sampling.minus2_log_likelihood` and reports `converged: false` in
two cases (#2652):

| Warning | Fires when |
|---|---|
| `W_NONFINITE_MARGINAL` | The marginal is `NaN`, infinite, or past the divergence cutoffs. This covers an `imp_eval_only` readout too, whatever the stage before it reported. |
| `W_MCEM_OBJECTIVE_ROSE` | The marginal sits above the lowest objective any iteration reached by more than 10% of that objective's magnitude, or of the observation count if that is larger. |

An EM iteration should not raise the objective, so the only legitimate gap
between the lowest iteration and the final marginal is Monte-Carlo noise. In a
seven-model comparison with NONMEM, measured on Linux, the widest gap on a healthy
run was 0.13% of that scale. The narrowest on a collapsed run, from before the
proposal-covariance fix of #2650 removed those collapses, was 51%. The baseline is the lowest iteration and not the first because a cold start begins far above the optimum: a
collapse can end below where it started and still be nowhere near the optimum.

The rise check needs an estimating IMP / IMPMAP stage and a published marginal. If
the marginal pass was skipped, a warning says so and this check does not run. The
marginal is computed after the last estimating stage, so a trailing `agq_eval_only`
readout replaces `ofv` and leaves both checks in force.

## Defensive mixture {#defensive-mixture}

A weakly-identified subject — e.g. an analytical `[initial_conditions]` baseline
whose `V` cancels in the amplitude — can produce a proposal so badly centred that
a *single* importance sample carries almost all the weight. That one sample then
hijacks the weighted M-step and walks θ to the parameter bounds; the run "diverges"
to a finite-but-enormous OFV. (This is issue #528; the OFV blow-up is now caught
by the convergence check, which flags an objective ≥ `1e15` as **not converged**
for both IMP/IMPMAP and SAEM.)

The optional **defensive mixture** (`imp_defensive_alpha`, default `0`) hardens the
sampler against this. With weight $\alpha \in [0,1)$ the proposal becomes

$$
q(\eta) = (1-\alpha)\,q_\text{narrow}(\eta) + \alpha\,q_\text{broad}(\eta),
$$

where $q_\text{broad} = \mathcal N(0, \Omega)$ is the prior (for the FREM
Rao-Blackwell path it is the *conditional* PK prior $\mathcal N(\mu, P_{pp}^{-1})$).
An $\alpha$ fraction of draws come from $q_\text{broad}$, and **every** sample is
scored under the full mixture density (the balance heuristic). Because the prior
provably covers the conditional posterior, this bounds each importance weight by
$p(y\mid\eta)/\alpha$, so no single sample can dominate — keeping the population
estimates identifiable even when the narrow proposal is poor.

Practical notes:

- **Opt-in for the MCEM iterations.** There the default `0` reproduces the
  single-proposal sampler **exactly** (same numbers, same RNG stream), like NONMEM,
  which has no defensive mixture. Enable it (e.g. `0.1`) only for models that
  exhibit the runaway above. A reported marginal is different: an
  [adaptive evaluation](#adaptive-evaluation) always keeps at least $\alpha = 0.1$.
- **It bounds the weights, not the raw ESS.** A sharp interior likelihood spike
  can still keep ESS low; the mixture only guarantees no single sample runs away.
- **Complementary to the ISCALE pilot search, not redundant with it.** The
  per-subject ISCALE search (`iscale_min`/`iscale_max`) already rescues *many*
  collapses by isotropically rebroadening a too-narrow proposal, and with it on the
  mixture is often unnecessary. But ISCALE applies a single scalar to the whole
  proposal covariance: it cannot cover a proposal that is badly *centred* or wrong
  in *shape* (anisotropic). The $\mathcal N(0,\Omega)$ mixture component covers the full
  prior support regardless of the narrow proposal's centre or shape, so it remains
  the guard of last resort when a scalar rescale is not enough. (On the #528
  analytical-`[initial_conditions]` fixture the two overlap — ISCALE alone now
  prevents the runaway — which is why the regression test pins ISCALE off to
  isolate the mixture's distinct contribution; see #961.)
- **ESS-floor side effect.** Roughly $\alpha$ of each subject's samples now come
  from the broad prior, which raises the per-subject ESS fraction. A genuinely
  weakly-identified subject that would have been listed under
  `imp_low_ess_threshold` may no longer trip it — read the low-ESS diagnostic with
  that in mind when $\alpha > 0$.
- **Sobol QMC still applies** while the mixture is active (#1965): with
  `impmap_sobol` / `imp_sobol` on, a dedicated quasi-random coordinate picks
  each draw's component, so the broad fraction is stratified (within one draw
  of αK when K is a power of two) instead of binomial, and both components take their normals from the
  same Sobol point. Under `imp_sobol` the Student-t proposal is limited to
  `imp_proposal_df ≤ 1000` (use `normal` beyond that) and a draw to 1000
  quasi-random coordinates; both are checked when the fit starts.
- For an IMPMAP stage the option may also be written `impmap_defensive_alpha`
  (an alias for the same field).

## SDE / [diffusion] models (not supported)

IMP refuses to run on models with a `[diffusion]` block. The EKF
process-noise variance that inflates the residual variance for SDE
models is not yet threaded through the IS observation-likelihood path,
so the marginal would be silently biased. Use FOCE / FOCEI for the
Laplace OFV on SDE models; IMP for SDE is tracked as a follow-up.

## IOV (inter-occasion variability)

> Both the estimating `imp` and evaluation-only `imp` support IOV. The
> estimating method samples the same joint (η, κ) vector each iteration and
> updates Ω~IOV~ in closed form — see [IMPMAP: inter-occasion
> variability](impmap.qmd#impmap-iov), whose E- and M-steps it shares (#2301).

For models with `kappa` declarations, IMP performs
**joint sampling** of
both η (between-subject variability) and κ (between-occasion variability).
The proposal is built from the full (n_eta + n_kappa × n_occasions)
posterior Hessian, and the IS weights include both the η and κ priors.

The result struct flags this via `kappa_treatment = "marginalized"`
(YAML) and the CLI prints a notice. The reported `−2 log L` integrates
over both η and κ uncertainty, making it directly comparable to
NONMEM `$EST METHOD=IMP LAPLACIAN=1` on κ.

## Standard errors on a non-Gaussian model

With a TTE, `[binary_model]` or CTMM endpoint, the covariance step after `imp` differentiates
the 7-node quadrature marginal (`method = laplace, n_agq = 7`) rather than the FOCEI objective,
whose minimum can sit far from the `imp` estimate on such a model (#1781). See
[SAEM: covariance step on a non-Gaussian model](saem.qmd#saem-covariance-non-gaussian) for
when it applies, the measured effect, and the warnings it carries.

## Cost

K × n_subjects predict calls per pass, and an evaluation runs
`imp_adapt_passes + 1` passes. For warfarin (32 subjects) with K=2000 and the
default 5 pilots this is ≈ 384k predicts — seconds to a minute on a typical
laptop. The cost is linear in K and trivially parallel over subjects
(uses the same Rayon worker pool as the inner loop).

## Output

In the CLI:

```
--- Importance Sampling (marginal log-likelihood) ---
  -2 log L (IS): 1284.52  (MC SE = 0.41, K = 2000, ν = 5)
  ESS / K: min = 0.18, median = 0.62
  Proposal adaptation: up to 5 pilot passes
  Low-ESS subjects (3): 12=0.18, 27=0.21, 34=0.22
```

In the fit YAML:

```yaml
importance_sampling:
  minus2_log_likelihood: 1284.524300
  mc_standard_error: 0.412700
  n_samples: 2000
  proposal_df: 5.0000
  ess_min: 0.1800
  ess_median: 0.6200
  adapt_passes: 5
  kappa_treatment: marginalized  # or not_applicable if no IOV
  low_ess_subjects:
    - id: "12"
      ess_fraction: 0.1800
    - id: "27"
      ess_fraction: 0.2100
    - id: "34"
      ess_fraction: 0.2200
```

The Rust `FitResult.importance_sampling` field carries the same data
typed as `Option<ImportanceSamplingResult>`.

## NONMEM comparison

ferx's estimating `imp` is validated against NONMEM 7.5.1 `METHOD=IMP` on the
warfarin example (10-subject extract, `data/warfarin.csv`). Both engines are
warm-started from a FOCE/FOCEI pass (ferx `method = [focei, imp]`; NONMEM
`$EST METHOD=COND INTERACTION` → `$EST METHOD=IMP INTERACTION NITER=100
ISAMPLE=1000 SEED=12345`, control stream `tests/nonmem/warfarin_imp.ctl`).

| Parameter | NONMEM `METHOD=IMP` | ferx `[focei, imp]` |
|-----------|--------------------:|--------------------:|
| TVCL      | 0.1264              | 0.1327              |
| TVV       | 7.723               | 7.737               |
| TVKA      | 0.8857              | 0.811               |
| ω²(CL)    | 0.0304              | 0.0286              |
| ω²(V)     | 0.0096              | 0.0096              |
| ω²(KA)    | 0.3405              | 0.336               |
| σ (SD)    | 0.0105              | 0.0106              |
| IMP marginal `−2 log L` | −285.69 | −285.93 ± 0.07 |
| Laplace `ofv`           | (−286.00 at COND) | −286.00 |

Both engines start from the same FOCEI basin (NONMEM `METHOD=COND` OFV −286.00,
identical to ferx's FOCEI). NONMEM's IMP MCEM then drifts slightly off it toward
the importance-sampled marginal optimum (TVKA up to 0.886), while ferx's
warm-started IMP holds near the FOCEI optimum — both stable and agreeing within
the cross-engine + Monte-Carlo margin. TVKA is the least-identified parameter on
this small extract (ETA_KA variance ≈ 0.34, high shrinkage); CL/V and the
variance components agree to a few percent.

Compare like with like: NONMEM's reported IMP `#OBJV` (−285.69) is the
importance-sampling **marginal** `−2 log L`, so the matching ferx number is
`importance_sampling.minus2_log_likelihood` (−285.93 ± 0.07), *not* ferx's
Laplace `ofv` (−286.00, which instead coincides with NONMEM's COND OBJ). The
small residual gap is the parameter-estimate difference (ferx's TVKA sits a
little below NONMEM's), not an OFV-definition difference — both objectives drop
the same `Nobs·log(2π)` constant (NONMEM "WITHOUT CONSTANT"). The cross-check
lives in `tests/warfarin_imp_nonmem.rs`.

## See also

- [SAEM](saem.qmd) — common upstream stage for `method = [saem, imp]` with
  `imp_eval_only = true`, which scores the SAEM fit (NONMEM `SAEM` →
  `IMP EONLY=1`); see [Post-SAEM Finalization](saem.qmd#post-saem-finalization).
- [SIR](sir.qmd) — a different importance-sampling-flavoured procedure
  that targets *parameter uncertainty* (CIs on θ/Ω/σ), not the marginal
  likelihood. The name overlap is unfortunate; the two methods are
  unrelated in goal and implementation.
